title: Distance and Change on the Number Line

steps.body: Subtraction finds the CHANGE between two values: new − old tells you how much something moved. A temperature going from -3° to 5°: 5 − (−3) = 8, a rise of 8 degrees.
Subtract on the line — the direction of the hops is the whole game.

widget.prompt: −3 − (−6): start at −3 and make 6 hops. You choose where they land.

commonLandings.feedback: You hopped LEFT 6 — that computes −3 − 6. Here we subtract NEGATIVE 6, so flip it to +6 and hop right instead.

widget.missFeedback: From −3, subtracting −6 means adding 6: count exactly six hops to the right and land on 3.
widget.successFeedback: −3 − (−6) = −3 + 6 = 3 — subtracting a negative walks you to the RIGHT.

predict.prompt: You'll compute −3 − (−6) with six hops from −3. Which way do the hops go?
predict.reveal: Subtracting −6 is adding its opposite, +6: six hops RIGHT from −3 land on 3. 'Subtract means go left' only holds when the number being taken away is positive — a negative flips the direction.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents subtract change.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for subtract change must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines subtract change.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

commonErrors.feedback: Subtracting a NEGATIVE flips to adding a positive: -8 − (−20) = -8 + 20 = 12.
The opposite of −20 is +20, and -8 + 20 = 12, not negative.

steps.body: A falling value gives a negative change. From 10 to 4: 4 − 10 = -6, a drop of 6.

commonErrors.feedback: 10 has the bigger magnitude and is now negative, so the answer is -6, not 6.

steps.body: Always subtract new minus old to find the change — the sign of the result tells you rise (positive) or fall (negative).

commonErrors.feedback: Subtracting a NEGATIVE flips to adding a positive: -2 − (−19) = -2 + 19 = 17.
The opposite of −19 is +19, and -2 + 19 = 17, not negative.
15 has the bigger magnitude and is now negative, so the answer is -12, not 12.
Subtracting a NEGATIVE flips to adding a positive: 6 − (−9) = 6 + 9 = 15.
The opposite of −9 is +9, and 6 + 9 = 15, not negative.
Subtracting a NEGATIVE flips to adding a positive: -5 − (−22) = -5 + 22 = 17.
The opposite of −22 is +22, and -5 + 22 = 17, not negative.

hints: The signs are now different: subtract magnitudes 22−5=17.
22 has the bigger magnitude and is positive, so the answer is 17.

steps.body: Subtraction (new − old) finds the change — positive means it rose, negative means it fell.
takeaways: A positive change means a rise; a negative change means a fall.
Rewriting as adding the opposite makes any change computable.
steps.teaser: next: mixing addition and subtraction in one problem.

concept.body: Change = new − old. A rise from -3 to 5: 5 − (−3) = 5 + 3 = 8. A fall from 10 to 4: 4 − 10 = -6.

commonErrors.feedback: Subtracting a negative flips to adding: -3+11=8.
Subtracting a negative adds. −3 − (−11) becomes −3 + 11 = 8, a positive.
